newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil range-bound despite IOC.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil range-bound despite IOC.

text.p: Singapore gas oil trading were range-bound late afternoon on Friday despite talk of lower than expected award in India's tender for March deliveries, traders said.
"The market appears to have bottomed. There is support at $26.00 (per barrel) and whenever offers near this level buyers emerge," one broker said.
February gas oil swaps traded at high of $26.25 a barrel in the morning but this afternoon deals were seen at $26.10 and $26.15, unchanged from late Thursday's quotes of $26.10/$26.25, brokers said.
February was last quoted at $26.00/$26.10, while March was quoted at $26.45/$26.60.
The February/March gas oil contango widened to minus 50/35 cents per barrel from late Thursday's traded level minus 30 cents.

Traders said the market was not reacting to expectations of a lower award by India for March delivery cargoes at between 500,000 and 600,000 tonnes, compared with initial estimates of between 600,000 and 900,000 tonnes.
"There are talks of new demand from China and Indonesia, may be this is keeping the market steady," one trader said.
The jet fuel/gas oil regrade was unchanged at the higher $2.60/$3.00 level for February compared to an early week traded level of $2.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil edged down slightly but traders said the market remained above the key $100.00 per tonne mark.
February fuel oil swaps was quoted at $100.00/$101.00, down from Thursday's $101.50/$102.50, with deals seen earlier today at $100.25, $101.50 and $102.00 per tonne.
